facts.claim: Hormesis defines the quantitative rules within which adaptive processes operate and determines the extent to which biological performance, such as lifespan, can be enhanced or extended.
facts.quote: Hormesis defines the quantitative rules within which adaptive processes operate and is central to evolution and biology... the extent to which biological performance (e.g. , memory, resistance to injury/disease, wound healing, hair growth or lifespan) can be enhanced/extended

facts.claim: Late life intervention was sufficient to yield a potent health benefit from the natural product fisetin.
facts.quote: Late life intervention was sufficient to yield a potent health benefit.

facts.claim: There is a greater than 99% probability that the current maximum reported age at death of 122 will be broken by 2100.
facts.quote: Based on the Bayesian analysis, there is a greater than 99% probability that the current MRAD of 122 will be broken by 2100.

facts.claim: The natural product fisetin has senotherapeutic activity in mice and in human tissues.
facts.quote: The natural product fisetin has senotherapeutic activity in mice and in human tissues.

rejected.claim: The probability that a person lives to at least age 126, 128, or 130 this century is estimated at 89%, 44%, and 13%, respectively.
rejected.quote: We estimate the probabilities that a person lives to at least age 126,128, or 130 this century, as 89%, 44%, and 13%, respectively.

research.angle: While there is a high probability that the current maximum human lifespan will be broken by 2100, the extent of this extension is governed by quantitative rules of hormesis and potential senotherapeutic interventions.
research.verdict: The evidence suggests that human lifespan is not currently capped at 122 and may be extendable through biological and pharmacological interventions.
research.caveat: The probability of reaching extreme ages like 130 remains relatively low at 13% according to current Bayesian projections.
